data.gender_notes: Hijrah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic history, Hijrah refers to the migration of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) from Mecca to Medina in 622 AD. This event marked the beginning of the Islamic calendar and signified a significant transformation in the spread of Islam. The name Hijrah carries the meaning “Migration, Journey” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hijrah usually hope their child will grow to embody migration, journey and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the spiritual journey towards enlightenment and a new beginning in life.
data.etymology: Hijrah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Migration, Journey.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hijrah total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The Hijrah event holds immense cultural significance as it represents the foundation of the Islamic state and community. Muhammad's (PBUH) decision to migrate led to the establishment of the first Muslim polity and the establishment of a local court system, giving Muslims a sense of collectivity and belonging. Additionally, the migration allowed the Prophet to expand the reach of Islam, leading to the conversion of numerous individuals and tribes, and setting the stage for the spread of Islam beyond the Arabian Peninsula.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the Hijrah marks the completion of a divine plan set in motion at Muhammad's (PBUH) birth. It is believed that Allah (SWT) had destined the Prophet to bring about a new way of life and a message of peace and equality to humanity. The migration to Medina symbolizes a journey towards a better way of life and obedience to Allah's commandments. It is also seen as an act of courage and determination, an inspiring example of faith and perseverance for Muslims today.
